scenario.title: BATTLE OF GRODNO - 20 SEP 1939
intro.text:
BATTLE OF GRODNO - 20 SEP 1939

Southeast of Grodno, East Poland

Move your units across the city of Grodno to the Lithuanian border. Occupy the city and vicinity and break any resistance!

ORDERS
a. Capture all VH!
b. Prevent that more than 2 enemy ground units cross the Polish-Lithuanian border (Exit Points).

CORE (recommended)
2x Tank
4x Infantry (+1)
2x Reconnaissance (+1)
2x Artillery (+1)
1x Fighter Aircraft
1x Tactical Bomber (+1)
header.location: Southeast of Grodno, eastern Poland — 20 September 1939
player.speaker: Commander
line.reaction-briliant.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.reaction-briliant.text: The Baintsagan bridgehead collapsed before its two thrusts could support one another. Moscow calls it proof of a modern operation, which guarantees that somebody will copy only the arrows.
line.reaction-victory.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.reaction-victory.text: Khalkhin Gol restored the river line and left the Japanese attack broken. It also left us a report thick enough to conceal every disagreement that produced the result.
line.reaction-tactical.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.reaction-tactical.text: We held the Mongolian line, but the steppe consumed enough vehicles to make the victory look smaller from the repair park than from headquarters.
line.callback-choice-a.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.callback-choice-a.text: At Baintsagan you sent the mobile force beyond the visible objective. The staff now treats deep exploitation as your signature; every ambitious lieutenant wants to imitate the part that appears on the map.
line.callback-choice-b.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.callback-choice-b.text: You rebuilt the river line before pursuing at Khalkhin Gol. It was less dramatic than the arrows Antonov proposed, and it left us a force still answering orders at the end.
line.scene-0.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.scene-0.text: The printed order calls this a march to secure the frontier. The road says otherwise: Polish soldiers, local militias, refugees, and Soviet columns are all moving through the same villages under different assumptions about who has authority.
line.scene-1.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.scene-1.text: The German liaison map ends at the same northern line as ours. I folded that overlay before the refugees entered. The line is easier to share than the road beneath it.
line.decision.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.decision.text: Resistance in Grodno can be bypassed only if the border routes are sealed early. We can lead with mobile groups and risk broken communications, or keep a coherent front and accept that more enemy units may reach Lithuania.
line.decision.choice.seal-the-border.tex: Send the mobile group past Grodno first and close the northern exits.
line.decision.choice.seal-the-border.hin: Give reconnaissance formations 25 experience, fully refuel the core, and gain 60 prestige for sealing the frontier roads.
line.decision.choice.control-the-advance: Clear the approaches in sequence and keep every formation under direct control.
Give infantry 20 experience and artillery 15 experience, and fully replenish ammunition without restoring fuel or strength.
line.choice-a-0.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.choice-a-0.text: The mobile group will not become an excuse for indiscriminate fire. It closes roads, reports movement, and leaves the city fight to the forces assigned to it.
line.choice-a-1.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.choice-a-1.text: I can assign roads, exits, and halting lines. I cannot mark every armed man in a refugee column from this table. Detached groups will make those decisions without us.
line.choice-b-0.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.choice-b-0.text: Then the advance moves on confirmed orders, not rumour. We may catch fewer columns, but no detached battalion is to invent its own war.
line.choice-b-1.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.choice-b-1.text: Confirmed orders will restrain detached battalions. They will not make this march innocent. I want the arrests, shootings, and released prisoners recorded under the units that ordered them.
line.post-0.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.post-0.text: Record what the map cannot: civilians on the roads, prisoners taken, and every order that prevented avoidable bloodshed.
